obligation: Acquirer notice of suspected card data compromise (contractual)
citation: Merchant agreement with the acquiring bank (fictional term); PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 12.10 (N44-45-R01)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise of card data, including a common point of purchase notice from the acquirer or processor
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspecting a compromise (merchant agreement term)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law

obligation: Card brand compromise reporting: Visa worked example (contractual)
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Sections A.1-A.3 and A.5; Visa Core Rules 10.3.1.2. Card brand rules applied through the acquirer, not law. If the business accepts American Express, the DSOP (April 2026, Section 3) requires notice to American Express within 72 hours of discovery. Mastercard and Discover rules not verified
trigger: Evidence sufficient to raise a reasonable suspicion of, or to confirm, unauthorized access to Visa account data or a system that stores, processes or transmits it
deadline: Tell the acquirer immediately (A.3.1). Make sure the event is reported to Visa within 3 calendar days of the suspicion or confirmation (A.1.1), then send the incident report within 3 calendar days of that notice (A.2.1). If Visa requires a PCI Forensic Investigator, retain one within 5 business days (A.5.1.1)
notify: Acquirer; Visa Global Risk Investigations, through the acquirer. Other brands as the acquirer directs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - follow acquirer instructions; Mastercard and Discover rules were not verified
clock_starts: Suspicion or confirmation of the compromise

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents. Personal information includes a name with a card number and any required security code, and an email address with a password for an online account (501.171(1)(g))
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and without unreasonable delay, no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - expected for skimmed cards with security codes, or for stolen account credentials
clock_starts: Determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred

obligation: Florida 15-day extension for individual notice
trigger: Good cause for delay of the individual notice
deadline: 15 additional days for the individual notice only, if good cause is provided in writing to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days after determination. Never extends the Department notice
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (written request)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if needed

obligation: Florida law enforcement delay
trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies; get the request in writing
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: Florida no-notice determination
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Document the determination, keep it 5 years, and provide it to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely for skimmed card data or ransomware with exfiltration; counsel decides

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after the determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A third-party agent (for example the e-commerce platform vendor, the marketing agency, or the offers engine vendor) has a breach of a system it maintains for the company
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days following the determination of the breach
notify: The company (Privacy and Compliance Manager); the company then gives the notices in (3) and (4)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in vendor contracts (POAM-012)

obligation: State data breach notification (other states)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of residents of other states (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example without unreasonable delay or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside (online customers and seasonal residents)

obligation: Supplier notice of compromise of supplier confidential data (contractual)
citation: Supplier offers and retail media agreements (fictional term)
trigger: Unauthorized access to supplier campaign or sales data in the reporting portal or data warehouse
deadline: Within 72 hours of confirming the incident (contract term)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law
owner: Director of E-commerce and Marketing with the General Counsel

obligation: Lender and private equity sponsor notice (contractual)
citation: Credit agreement and sponsor reporting terms (fictional)
trigger: Material cyber incident or extended outage
deadline: Within 5 business days (credit agreement term)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement
trigger: Suspected criminal compromise of card data, ransomware, or extortion
deadline: As soon as practical (target day 0-2)
notify: FBI (IC3) or U.S. Secret Service field office
applies_at_this_tier: Recommended; supports any later OFAC review

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy: use the carrier breach hotline before engaging any incident vendor
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering any ransom or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if a demand is made. All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties
owner: Chief Executive Officer with outside counsel

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule notification event (unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted customer information)
trigger: Notification event at a financial institution involving 500 or more consumers
deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 30 days after discovery
notify: FTC via online form at ftc.gov
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company issues no credit and is not a financial institution under 16 CFR Part 314

obligation: Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident disclosure
trigger: Registrant determines an incident is material
deadline: Within four business days after determining the incident is material
applies_at_this_tier: No - privately held

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). Proposed scope: critical infrastructure entities above the SBA size standard, or meeting a sector criterion regardless of size; the company exceeds its SBA size standard, so coverage would turn on the final rule's critical infrastructure sector definitions

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts

obligation: Kaspersky covered article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies a Kaspersky covered article in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts
